chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-'Amriki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the crumbs/dregs from sugar, almonds, and similar things, whether it is permissible to eat them. He said: 'It is disliked to eat what has been gathered/cleaned up.'

key_terms.اُنْتُهِبَ: Was gathered/cleaned up (from the verb nathaba)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the leftover crumbs from sugar or nuts according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on consuming *nuthar* (leftover crumbs or dregs) from foods like sugar and almonds, declaring it *makruh* specifically when it is gathered or cleaned up from the place of consumption. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and avoiding the appearance of scavenging or excessive frugality that might detract from dignity during meals. The distinction highlights the nuanced approach of the Imams in balancing permissibility with recommended social conduct.
